candidates.exact_span: Input pollutant geometric mean concentration as micro-gram per liter (ug/l or ppb) unless other unit is specified for the parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether limits and reported measurements are compared in ug/l/ppb or another unit changes which numeric limit is applicable and whether a reported value exceeds it.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) but the DL is greater than MQL, input "1/2 DL" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigning 1/2 DL as the effluent concentration for calculations changes the effective value used in limit derivation and compliance comparison, and determines whether a non-detect is treated as a usable numeric input versus a missing-data state.

candidates.exact_span: Effluent value reported as "< detection level" (DL) and the DL is smaller than MQL, no data is inputted.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Treating sub-MQL non-detects as no data input changes whether an enforceable numeric comparison can be performed and how the absence of a numeric result is classified (no-data versus substitute value).

candidates.exact_span: If a less than MQL vakue is reported, input either the reported value or "0" for calculation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The discretionary choice between the reported less-than-MQL value and zero changes calculated concentrations and compliance outcomes, and leaves ambiguous how such reports should be semantically classified when no ordinary numeric result is available.

Different interpretation of the instream waste concentration formula or its inputs (including the 2.13 multiplier on effluent concentration) yields different derived concentration limits against which effluent measurements are compared.

candidates.exact_span: F = Fraction of stream allow ed for mixing (see "Procedures for Implementing NPDES Permits in New Mexico")
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mixing fraction F is a direct input to instream waste concentration calculation; uncertainty about which F value applies from the referenced procedures changes the applicable numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: Qa = Critical low flow of stream at discharge point expressed as the 4Q3 or harmonic mean flow for human health criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selection between 4Q3 and harmonic mean flow for Qa alters dilution assumptions in limit derivation and therefore which enforceable numeric limit applies.

candidates.exact_span: The follow ing formular convert metals reported in total form to dissolved form if criteria are in dissolved form
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when total-metal measurements must be converted to dissolved form before comparison determines which numeric dissolved criterion is applicable.
The partition conversion formula governs how total metal criteria are translated to dissolved limits; different interpretation of Kp or TSS inputs changes the applicable dissolved numeric limit.

candidates.exact_span: TSS = Total suspended solids concentration found in receiving stream (or in effluent for intermittent stream)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether TSS is taken from the receiving stream or from effluent for intermittent streams changes Kp and thus the derived dissolved metal limit used in compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Stream Linear Partition Coefficient                                                             Lake Linear Partition Coefficient
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether stream or lake partition coefficients apply changes Kpo, alpha, Kp, and C/Ct values and therefore the dissolved limits derived for total metal parameters.

The stream dissolved value of 0 for Chromium III implies a zero dissolved criterion after conversion; interpretation of this table entry changes whether any reported chromium measurement can exceed an applicable limit.

candidates.exact_span: The follow ing formular is used to calculate hardness dependent criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Hardness-dependent criteria are not fixed numeric limits; applicability of these formulas versus tabulated values determines which enforceable limit applies to hardness-sensitive parameters.

candidates.exact_span: Aluminum (T)                                      Acute                                  e(1.3695[ln(hardness)]+1.8308)                               5003.02112                 If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 750 in cell O113
candidates.computation_change_reason: The acute aluminum limit depends on hardness unless stream pH is below 6.5, in which case a fixed value of 750 applies; interpretation of the pH condition changes the applicable acute limit.

candidates.exact_span: Chronic                                e(1.3695[ln(hardness)]+0.9161)                              2004.394367                 If Stream pH < 6.5, enter 87 in cell P113
candidates.computation_change_reason: The chronic aluminum limit depends on hardness unless stream pH is below 6.5, in which case a fixed value of 87 applies; interpretation of the pH condition changes the applicable chronic limit.
The acute cadmium limit is computed from hardness through CF1; different interpretation of hardness or the CF1 formula changes the applicable acute numeric limit.
The chronic cadmium limit is computed from hardness through CF2; different interpretation of hardness or the CF2 formula changes the applicable chronic numeric limit.
